checklist.starterNeedsUpdate: Update Bug Detective to start playing. The first project needs a newer version of the app.
checklist.title: Before you start
checklist.intro: Bug Detective runs SupportDesk in Docker and opens it in your own VS Code. Let's check that everything is installed.

docker.title: Docker Desktop
docker.notInstalled: Docker Desktop is not installed. Install it with the WSL 2 backend, then come back.
docker.notRunning: Docker Desktop is installed but not running.
docker.starting: Docker Desktop is starting. This can take a minute.

wsl.title: WSL 2
wsl.notFound: WSL is not installed. Open PowerShell as administrator and run: wsl --install
wsl.wsl1Only: Only WSL 1 was found. Docker Desktop needs WSL 2: run wsl --set-default-version 2

vscode.title: Visual Studio Code
vscode.cliNotFound: VS Code was not found. Install it (the default options are fine), then check again.

devcontainers.title: Dev Containers extension
devcontainers.ok: The Dev Containers extension is installed.
devcontainers.extensionMissing: VS Code needs the Dev Containers extension to open the code inside the container.
devcontainers.checkFailed: Could not list the VS Code extensions. Try again.

banner.dockerStopped: Docker is not running. Actions that need it are paused until it is back.

dashboard.projectNeedsUpdate: Update Bug Detective: this project needs a newer version of the app. You can keep playing with what is already downloaded.
dashboard.previousDirective: You are viewing the directive for a previous ticket ({{key}}, done). Your active assignment is {{active}}.
dashboard.previousDirectiveNoActive: You are viewing the directive for a ticket you already finished ({{key}}).
dashboard.genericAssignmentBody: A new ticket is waiting for you. Open it on the Board when you are ready.
dashboard.unlocking: Downloading and setting up the ticket…
dashboard.blockedDockerBody: Start Docker Desktop to download your next ticket. Your previous fixes are safe.
dashboard.dockerDownActive: Docker is not running. VS Code and the app open again once it is back.
dashboard.allDoneBody: Your board and your code are still here to explore.
dashboard.queuedBody: Your next ticket is ready to download.
dashboard.downloadFirst: Download the game environment to continue. After that, the game works offline.
dashboard.nextTitle: Next action: get your next assignment
dashboard.nextBody: The ticket is downloaded and your workspace is set up for it. One ticket at a time.
dashboard.chooseTrack: Choose the track of the next ticket

installModal.title: Downloading the game environment
installModal.running: Downloading and installing. The first time this can take several minutes.

welcome.title: Welcome to the team!
welcome.body: Hi! I'm Rafaela, engineering manager here at {{company}}. Before your first ticket, I'll do your onboarding: a quick tour of the Dashboard and the Board, where you'll work. It takes about 2 minutes.

closing.title: That's it!
closing.body: Your first ticket is ready: on the Dashboard, click Get next assignment to start. Any questions, Priya is your mentor: ask her from the ticket.
closing.bodyReplay: Any questions, Priya is your mentor: ask her from the ticket.

currentTask.title: Current task
currentTask.body: This is the ticket you're working on. When I hand you a ticket, it shows up here, with the button that takes you to it and shortcuts to VS Code and the browser.

environment.title: Local environment
environment.body: Docker, the images and the dev server SupportDesk runs on. When something needs your attention, the title turns red and the item tells you what to do.

client.title: Client, project and contacts
client.body: Who we're building SupportDesk for. Under Project & contacts you'll find the project and the team: Priya, the senior developer, is your mentor.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.body: This is how I send you your tasks. Each new ticket arrives here as an e-mail from me.

message.title: The open e-mail
message.body: Read the request here. When a new task is waiting, the e-mail shows the Pick up next task button.

board.title: The Board
board.body: The work on each ticket happens on the Board. Let's go there now.

columns.title: Columns and flow
columns.body: Every ticket goes through To Do, In Progress, In QA, Code Review and Done. You move it forward as the work progresses.

card.title: The ticket card
card.body: Click a card to see the ticket's details. The Move button (or a drag) takes it to the next column.

qa.title: In QA
qa.body: Drop the ticket here when you think it's fixed: the automated tests run. If something fails, the ticket comes back with the errors.

ticketOpen.title: The open ticket
ticketOpen.body: Click a card and the ticket opens here, beside the board, with everything you need to work on it. This one is just an example.

ticketHeader.title: Key, stage and title
ticketHeader.body: At the top are the ticket's key, the stage it is in and its title.

ticketActions.title: Code, app and dev server
ticketActions.body: Open in VS Code connects your editor to the code. Open app in browser shows SupportDesk running. The button below starts or stops the dev server.

ticketTab.title: The Ticket tab
ticketTab.body: Here is the request: what happens, how to reproduce it and what should happen. Always start by reproducing the bug.

qaTab.title: The QA tab
qaTab.body: Every time the ticket goes through QA, the result shows up here. If it fails, you see which tests broke and why.

historyTab.title: The History tab
historyTab.body: The history keeps your QA attempts and every move of the ticket.

seniorTab.title: Talking to Priya
seniorTab.body: Stuck? Ask Priya. She answers with one hint at a time and, after all of them, can show you the solution.

review.title: Code Review and Done
review.body: Once QA passes, compare your solution with the reference one in Code Review, then accept it to finish the ticket.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Language, theme, the status of your tools and the backup of your progress live here. No need to change anything now.

replay.title: See this again
replay.body: If you want to go through this onboarding again, just click here, at any time.

demo.title: Example: the search ignores capital letters
demo.ticketMarkdown:
## What happens

Searching for `login` finds the ticket, but searching for `Login` finds nothing.

## How to reproduce

1. Open the ticket list.
2. Search for `Login`.

## Expected

The search finds the same tickets, whatever the capital letters.
demo.question: I can reproduce it, but I don't know where to start.
demo.hint: Compare the two searches in the Network tab: what does the server receive in each one?

board.title: Board
board.hint: Move your ticket to In QA when the fix is ready. QA runs the project's tests first, then the ticket's own checks.
board.hintTodo: Move your ticket to In Progress and start your task.
board.hintCodeReview: Review and accept the code review to move the ticket to Done.
board.hintDone: Go back to the Dashboard and wait for your next assignment.
board.notAllowed: Only QA and the code review move a card there.
board.notAllowedInQa: Your card is being tested. When QA finishes, it moves the card to the right column.
board.notAllowedInReview: To move the card to Done, accept the code review.
board.notAllowedBackToTodo: Tickets in progress cannot go back to To Do.

emptyColumn.todo: Nothing waiting. New assignments arrive in your inbox.
emptyColumn.inProgress: Drag your ticket here when you start working on it.
emptyColumn.inQa: Drop your ticket here to run QA.
emptyColumn.codeReview: Tickets that pass QA wait here for review.
emptyColumn.done: Tickets land here once you accept their review.

board.solvedBug: The reference fix is now in your code. Move the card to In QA to test it.

ticket.devServerUp: The app is running. Stop it here to free its ports, or to restart it after changing settings.
ticket.devServerDown: The app is not running. Run npm run dev in the VS Code terminal, or start it here.
ticket.readOnly: This ticket is done. It is read-only.

senior.intro: {{name}} is happy to help. Hints come one at a time, from general to specific.
senior.question: Hi {{name}}, I'm stuck on this one. Could you point me in the right direction?
senior.solutionQuestion: I tried the hints and I'm still stuck. Could you walk me through the fix?
senior.solutionIntro: Here is how the reference fix works. You still need to apply it in your workspace and pass QA.
senior.onlyInProgress: Move the card to In Progress to ask for help.
senior.noMoreHints: No more hints. You can ask for the full solution.

ticket.vscodeHint: VS Code opens attached to the workspace container. If a VS Code window for this workspace is already open but disconnected (after an update or a restore), close it or run "Developer: Reload Window" in it.

comment.gate1Failed: Existing functionality broke. Your change made project tests fail. Fix them before resubmitting.
comment.gate2Failed: The reported bug is still unresolved. The app still shows the behavior described in the ticket.
comment.timeout: Timeout: QA exceeded the time limit of {{seconds}} seconds, possibly because of a hang or infinite loop.
comment.interrupted: QA was interrupted because the app closed. This does not count as an attempt. Move the card to In QA again.
comment.error: QA could not run. This does not count as an attempt. Details: {{detail}}
comment.branchWarning: Heads-up: your workspace is not on this ticket's code (it was switched in Git). QA evaluates the current files anyway.

qa.running: QA is running for this ticket. It cannot be cancelled.

review.title: Code review
review.comparison: Diff: your solution with the proposed solution
review.comparisonIntro: Your approved solution next to the reference solution. Both can be valid: use the differences to see other ways to solve the ticket.
review.identical: Your solution is identical to the reference
review.baselineIntro: Your changes compared with the code the ticket started from:

vscodeSteps.title: How to see the diff in VS Code
vscodeSteps.graph: In the Graph section, click the top commit, "Your approved solution" (below it is "Reference", the proposed solution). If Graph is not shown: "…" at the top of Source Control → Views → Graph.
vscodeSteps.diff: The diff of every file opens: the proposed solution on the left, yours on the right. The files are read-only.
vscodeSteps.back: When you are done, come back here and click "Back to my code" (your code also comes back on its own before QA).

review.startsDocker: Docker Desktop is not running: it starts first.
review.banner: Viewing the review of ticket {{ticket}} in VS Code. Your code will be restored automatically.

notice.editsSaved: Changes made while viewing the review of ticket {{ticket}} were saved separately and your code was restored.
notice.workKept: Your code was restored. Your work in progress was kept as a commit, because new commits were made while the review of ticket {{ticket}} was open.

review.referenceSection: Diff: proposed solution with the original code
review.referenceIntro: What {{name}} changed in the code the ticket started from to fix the bug.
review.doneNext: Ticket done! Go to the Dashboard to get your next task.
review.doneLast: Ticket done! That was the last one.

comparison.noLineChanges: Only the name or the file mode changed.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Manage your preferences, check your developer tools and keep your progress safe.
settings.languageHelp: Changes the app and the directives you receive from management.
settings.themeHelp: Pick a look, or follow your operating system.
settings.qaTimeoutHelp: How long an automated QA run may take before it stops.
settings.environmentHelp: The tools Bug Detective needs to run SupportDesk in a dev container.
settings.diskHelp: Space the game's Docker images and volumes take on this computer.

qaCache.name: QA dependency cache
qaCache.help: npm packages for offline QA runs

settings.diskNeedsDocker: Start Docker to measure disk usage.
settings.backupHelp: Your work lives in a Docker volume. A Docker reset deletes it, so export a save file from time to time.
settings.needsDocker: Start Docker to export or restore your progress.

locked.title: Actions locked: {{task}}
locked.body: Export, restore and new game are paused until it finishes.

tasks.removingDocker: everything is being removed from Docker
tasks.applyingCatalog: the development settings are being applied

settings.dangerZoneHelp: Start over from the first ticket. The board, history and hints are reset; the code in your workspace is archived, not deleted.
settings.newGameWarning: Your board, completed tickets and current assignment will be reset, and you start again from the first ticket. Export your progress first if you want to keep a copy. Code in the workspace is archived, not deleted.
settings.restoreWarning: This replaces your current progress and the workspace Docker volume. Uncommitted and unexported work will be lost.
settings.restoringHelp: Rebuilding the workspace volume and repository. Do not close Bug Detective.
settings.aboutTagline: An offline desktop game for developers who want to practice debugging real code.

cleanup.leftoversHelp: Removes what the game leaves behind in Docker: QA containers, the copy of your code that QA tested and images of older versions. Your code and progress stay.
cleanup.needsDocker: Docker is not running: start it to clean up. If Docker Desktop is stuck, restart it.
cleanup.everythingHelp: Deletes every container, volume and image Bug Detective created in Docker, including the code in your workspace, and starts a new game. Use it when Docker is left in a bad state.
cleanup.confirmWarning: This deletes the code in your workspace and starts a new game. It cannot be undone.
cleanup.confirmContainers: Containers: your workspace and any QA run left behind
cleanup.confirmVolumes: Volumes: your code, the VS Code server, the dependency cache and the QA copy
cleanup.confirmImages: Images: the workspace and QA images (about 4 GB, built again on the next download)
cleanup.confirmBackup: To keep your progress, cancel and export it first; you can restore it afterwards.
cleanup.everythingDone: Everything Bug Detective created in Docker was removed. A new game has started.
cleanup.partial_one: {{removed}} removed. Docker could not remove 1 item:
cleanup.partial_other: {{removed}} removed. Docker could not remove {{count}} items:
cleanup.restartHint: If Docker Desktop seems stuck, restart it (or your computer) and run the cleanup again.
cleanup.gameKept: Your progress was kept: the volume with your code could not be removed.

dev.title: Development
dev.help: Where this copy of the app reads its projects from. Saved in {{file}}; editing that file by hand is the same.
dev.testFile: BUGDETECTIVE_CATALOG_FILE is set, so it decides the catalog and these settings cannot be applied.
dev.error: The settings file could not be used: {{message}}. Apply to replace it.
dev.fallback: The chosen catalog has not been downloaded or read yet, so the app is using the copy bundled with this build.
dev.sourceHelp: The list of projects the app offers.
dev.projectsHelp: Where each project of the catalog in use gets its tickets and story.
dev.nextTicket: Changes apply from the next ticket. The open ticket keeps the version it was unlocked with.

errors.dockerUnavailable: Docker is not running. Start Docker Desktop and try again.
errors.environmentNotReady: Install the missing downloads on the Dashboard first.
errors.busy: Please wait for the current task to finish.
errors.hintsRemaining: Ask for the remaining hints first.
errors.noReview: The review of this ticket is not available.
errors.reviewFailed: The review could not be opened, and your code was restored: {{message}}
errors.vscodeFailed: VS Code could not be opened, and your code was restored: {{message}}
errors.solveBugNotAllowed: Only the ticket in progress can be solved.
errors.incompletePublication: The project's publication is incomplete. Try again later.
errors.switchIncomplete: The project switch is not finished: {{message}}
errors.appTooOld: This project needs a newer version of Bug Detective. Update the app to play it.
errors.reviewUnavailable: This PR was made before you switched projects, so it can only be reviewed in the app.
errors.switchInProgress: Finish the current project switch first.
errors.contentNeedsInternet: Connect to the internet to download the project.

projects.needsUpdate: Update Bug Detective to play this project.
projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Pick your next project. Only one project stays on your computer: switching removes the current one from Docker and downloads the next. Your progress and PRs are kept.
projects.noDetails: Connect to the internet to see the details.
projects.busy: Wait for the current task to finish.
projects.confirmRemoved: The current project leaves your computer: its code in Docker, its images and its dependencies are removed.
projects.confirmKept: Your progress, completed tickets and PRs are kept, and you can come back later (it is downloaded again). Export a backup first if you want a copy of your code.

search.label: Search projects
search.placeholder: Search by name, stack or skill
search.emptyBody: Try another search term or difficulty.

switch.pendingTitle: The project switch is not finished
switch.pendingBody: Docker still has resources of the previous project. Nothing else can start until they are removed.
